chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was brought a pickpocket who had snatched dirhams from the sleeve of a man. So he said: “If he snatched them from his outer shirt, I would not cut his hand; but if he snatched them from his inner shirt, I would cut it.”

key_terms.بِطَرَّارٍ: a pickpocket or one who stealthily snatches from clothing
key_terms.دَرَاهِمَ: silver coins; money taken in the theft
key_terms.قَطَعْتُهُ: I would cut his hand; meaning apply the hadd punishment for theft
key_terms.قَمِيصِهِ الدَّاخِلِ: his inner shirt or inner garment beneath the outer one
key_terms.قَمِيصِهِ الْأَعْلَى: his outer shirt or upper garment
key_terms.كُمِّ: the sleeve from which the money was taken

ai.seo_question: When is the hadd punishment applied for stealing money from a person’s clothing?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding theft and the hadd punishment. It distinguishes between taking from an outer garment and from an inner garment, showing that the legal ruling depends on the degree of protected concealment of the stolen property.
